forecasts.label: Capital financing requirement
forecasts.note: Restated at each quarterly return. The Q4 restatement comes from the annual return itself, so it lands on the outturn by construction — the interesting movement is Q1 to Q3.

forecasts.label: Interest payable
forecasts.note: The council's own full-year forecast, restated at each quarterly return.

forecasts.label: Revenue spending (net current expenditure)
forecasts.note: The full-year forecast of net current expenditure — the running cost of services — restated each quarter against the same measure at outturn.

forecasts.label: Capital expenditure
forecasts.note: Total capital spending forecast each quarter (the capital payments return) against the annual capital outturn. Capital spending not met from grants or receipts is what turns into new borrowing, so a forecast running ahead of outturn is a borrowing signal.

in_year.label: Interest payable, as reported each quarter
in_year.note: Per quarter, not cumulative. The quarterly return is a lighter collection than the annual one and sums to roughly 92% of it nationally, so the two are shown apart rather than added together.

news_drafts.headline: Bolton to use £30m reserves over three years to bridge budget gap
news_drafts.lead: Bolton Council is planning to use £30m from its reserves over three years ending 2027 to bridge funding gaps, according to its medium-term financial strategy. The Audit Committee heard that external auditors have characterised the planned drawdown as "unsustainable reliance on reserves and a lack of action to address the underlying reasons for persistent overspending". Auditors identified that asset ceiling interest of £31.5m had not been included in the council's pension accounting, requiring a revised actuary report. They also raised control weaknesses across asset management and governance, including a failure to maintain the Corporate Risk Register during 2023–24. The council is receiving support from Manchester and Salford councils on internal audit delivery while developing a resource strategy to address staffing constraints.

news_drafts.headline: Bolton forecasts £10.5m overspend on schools grant for special needs in 2026-27, with a DfE plan pending
news_drafts.lead:
Bolton expects to spend £10.5m more than its dedicated schools grant (the government grant that funds schools) in 2026-27, according to first-quarter monitoring papers for the council's Schools Forum. The whole of the overspend falls on high needs, the part of school funding for children with special educational needs and disabilities.

The council forecasts high needs spending of £72.409m against a net budget of £61.869m. Schools' delegated budgets, the money passed directly to individual schools, are on plan. Adding this year's overspend to deficits carried forward, the central reserve for the grant (money set aside, here in deficit) is projected at negative £29.745m at 31 March 2027.

Bolton has submitted a plan to reform special educational needs provision to the Department for Education. The department's decision on it will determine whether Bolton receives a High Needs Sustainability Grant to address the deficit. The papers show a potential grant of £10.539m, matching the forecast overspend. Neither approval nor an award has yet been confirmed.

findings.headline: No significant governance issues identified for 2025-26, despite identified improvement opportunities in audit resources, risk management, and procurement.
findings.detail: The council's review of governance effectiveness has not identified any significant governance issues to report for the year ended March 2026. The council notes it continues to monitor and respond to a range of wider risks including significant financial challenges, changes in service demand, inflation, supply chain risks, workforce capacity, and new legislation.
findings.matters: A positive assurance position on governance frameworks provides confidence in the council's control environment. This is relevant context for a lender assessing whether identified improvement areas represent governance breakdown or normal continuous improvement.
findings.quote: The review process has not identified any significant governance issues necessary to highlight in this statement but there are challenges and opportunities that may impact on future ways of working and governance arrangements that continue to be reflected in the AGS Development Plan.

findings.headline: Audit assessment found gaps in Procurement Act compliance; consistency of commissioning practice across council needs improvement.
findings.detail: An audit assessment of Procurement Act compliance identified that while some areas show strong commissioning and procurement practice, there is a need for greater assurance over the consistency of approach across all council activities. An improvement plan will be delivered in 2026-27, informed by a follow-up internal audit review, with the initial assessment reporting by December 2026.
findings.matters: Procurement governance gaps represent financial control risk and may indicate inconsistent value-for-money assurance across the council's spending, a core concern for both finance directors and lenders.
findings.quote: An audit assessment of compliance with the Procurement Act and management's own review of arrangements conformed that there are further steps that could be taken to ensure visibility and governance of procurement activity across the Council.

findings.headline: Audit found information governance oversight needs strengthening; Business Improvement Review underway.
findings.detail: Internal Audit and management reviews identified opportunities to strengthen oversight of information governance arrangements across the council and to ensure directorate engagement in information governance standards and compliance. A Business Improvement Review is underway to assess approach and structures, reporting by December 2026.
findings.matters: Weak information governance oversight creates data security and regulatory compliance risks that could expose the council to operational disruption and reputational damage, both concerns for lenders assessing resilience.
findings.quote: Internal Audit and management reviews have confirmed opportunities to strengthen the oversight of information governance arrangements across the Council to both strengthen corporate functions and ensure engagement of directorates and departments in information governance standards and compliance

findings.headline: Risk management framework inconsistently applied at strategic and directorate level, and not regularly updated.
findings.detail: The council identified that its risk management strategy and framework for reviewing strategic and directorate-level risks has been inconsistent and outdated. A new Risk Management Strategy has been agreed by the Corporate Leadership Team and Audit Committee, with risks now managed via SharePoint and integrated into dashboards. However, the regularity of review needs to be embedded over a full year cycle before effectiveness is confirmed.
findings.matters: Inconsistent and outdated risk management reduces the council's structured visibility of emerging risks to service delivery and financial stability, which a lender would expect to be actively managed.
findings.quote: Risk management strategy and framework for review of risks at strategic and directorate level is inconsistent and has not been updated on a regular basis.

findings.headline: Internal Audit resources significantly reduced, limiting delivery of the planned annual audit programme.
findings.detail: Internal audit capacity has experienced significant reductions in staffing. This has constrained the council's ability to deliver its full annual audit plan as reported to the Audit Committee. A resourcing strategy is being developed to address the shortfall, including exploring shared resources from other councils and options to strengthen the service, with proposals to be shared by end September 2026.
findings.matters: Reduced audit capacity weakens the council's ability to provide assurance over financial controls and governance. A lender assessing the control environment needs to know whether internal audit has sufficient resources to identify control weaknesses.
findings.quote: Internal Audit resources are reduced significantly and this has limited the ability to deliver the annual audit plan as reported to Audit Committee.
